issues: Whether the passport program had a duty to disclose all material adverse evidence — including facial recognition comparison results, police and provincial investigator emails, an incomplete internal investigation report, and references to criminal charges — to the applicant before making a revocation decision
Whether a passport revocation and multi-year refusal of services can stand where material adverse evidence was not disclosed to the applicant before the decision was made
The standard of review applicable to a passport director's decision to revoke a passport and refuse passport services
Whether the decision was procedurally fair, including the duty to give reasons, the duty to allow a meaningful opportunity to respond, and the duty to disclose material adverse evidence
Whether the decision was substantively reasonable — whether the evidence, including facial recognition results and criminal charges, supported the finding of false or misleading information
The legal basis and scope of the director's power to revoke a passport and refuse passport services under the Passport Act
Whether the multi-year refusal of passport services is a proportionate response to the alleged conduct
key_facts: Client held a Canadian passport in the name he has used for years and renewed it without difficulty
Federal passport authority opened an investigation after a provincial ID office flagged him
Letters stated the authority believed he obtained the passport by giving false or misleading information under an assumed identity
Client also stood charged with an indictable offence for breaching a release condition
Letters set out a summary of findings and invited him to respond
He replied with a superior court order permitting delayed birth registration, the resulting birth registration, and a sworn declaration, all in the name he uses
A second letter told him his material did not neutralize the findings
The director revoked the passport and cut him off from passport services for about five years
The full record produced for the court challenge contained facial recognition comparison results that matched his photo to passports in his current name but not to earlier passports in the other name

The record also contained police and provincial investigator emails, an incomplete internal investigation report, and references to several other criminal charges that were never put to him in either letter
causes_of_action: Judicial review of passport revocation and refusal of services
